messages:
anna (support): customer reporting intermittent malformed JSON from our /v1/generate endpoint when using response_format=structured_json & strict=true. parser error: 'Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0'

anna (support): they sent a few responses that start with HTML ("<html>") then a truncated JSON payload. happens ~1/10 requests. also saw a 502 earlier.

mike (eng-api): can you paste repro curl and headers? also need request-id from the response if available.

anna (support): here's the curl they used:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -H 'Accept: application/json' \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b", "input":"summarize:", "response_format":"structured_json", "strict":true}'
```

anna (support): example response body (from customer):
```
<html><body>502 Bad Gateway</body></html>{
  "choices": [
    {"text":"..."},
  ]
}
```

ryan (eng-runtime): hm looks like an upstream gateway HTML error got concatenated before the JSON. could be proxy returning an HTML error page while the backend stream resumed. do we have edge logs for their Request-ID?

anna (support): customer didn't see a request-id header. they said after rotating the API key they saw auth failures earlier: 401 then later these mangled responses started.

ryan (eng-runtime): that matches a hypothesis: auth rotation -> short-lived 401 from auth-proxy -> proxy injected HTML error body for some chunked responses and then backend resumed streaming JSON, so the client sees HTML + JSON and strict parser fails.

mike (eng-api): can they reproduce with verbose headers? ask them to add `-D -` to curl so we capture headers. also add `-H "X-Debug-Session: <id>"` so we can grep in logs.

anna (support): asked customer to repro and include raw response + headers. gave them a temporary L2 contact window.

sara (billing): FYI customer mentioned they hit a billing interruption a few hours before; could be correlated with key rotation or plan change. not sure if related.

ryan (eng-runtime): if we can get request-id and timestamp we can search edge logs for HTML responses around that time. possible mitigation: make strict mode enforcement prefer rejecting if Content-Type != application/json earlier (return 422) rather than streaming and risking concatenation. but need to verify root cause.

mike (eng-api): sounds actionable. steps: 1) get raw headers + response from customer, 2) if we find proxy HTML bodies in logs correlate with auth or billing events, 3) patch proxy to drop HTML bodies for streaming endpoints (or set content-type) and 4) add a guard in strict mode to reject on non-json content-type before streaming.

anna (support): customer provided sample headers in DM: `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8`, `Server: edge-proxy`, no `x-request-id`. forwarded to ryan + mike.

ryan (eng-runtime): I'll grep edge logs for that customer IP + timestamp range. also adding an alert to the streaming proxy team. ops-bot, can you create an incident ticket for potential streaming HTML injection?

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1842 - "edge-proxy HTML in streaming responses causing strict-json parse failures". assigned to eng-runtime and eng-api.

mike (eng-api): temporary workaround for customer: remove strict=true or set response_format to plain text and handle parsing defensively until we ship a fix. explain it's a safety tradeoff.

anna (support): relayed workaround. customer ok to toggle strict off but prefers a real fix. requesting ETA.

ryan (eng-runtime): initial triage: likely 1-2 days to root cause & patch proxy; if we need to alter API behavior (reject on content-type mismatch) expect a short follow-up release 3-5 days. i'll update thread once I have logs.

mike (eng-api): also logging follow-up: add stronger Content-Type enforcement for structured outputs, and make Accept header precedence explicit in docs. low-risk change for next deploy.

anna (support): thanks — will keep customer updated. tagging for escalation if we see more reports: @mike (eng-api) @ryan (eng-runtime) @sara (billing).

ryan (eng-runtime): found multiple hits in the edge for that IP and time window. there are HTML 502 fragments from auth-proxy during a key rotation event. attaching logs to INC-2026-1842.

anna (support): passing to customer: confirmed cause = auth-proxy returned HTML for a subset of chunked streams during API key rotation, which got concatenated with subsequent JSON.

anna (support): customer accepts workaround (strict=false) for now; asked for ETA for permanent fix.

ryan (eng-runtime): marking incident as P2. working on proxy patch & adding a strict-mode preflight check (reject if Content-Type header != application/json). will update in incident.

sara (billing): also following up internally on the billing/key-rotation path to avoid unexpected key state transitions during active streaming sessions.

mike (eng-api): documenting mitigation and a short note in docs about strict mode: clients should verify Content-Type and consider tolerant parsing if they cannot guarantee no mid-stream auth events.

anna (support): closing customer loop; they'll re-open if they see it again. keeping incident open until patch deployed.

ops-bot: incident INC-2026-1842 status -> investigating
